blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Unit 2 (Functions and Graphs), arranged by the unit's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each one is solved briefly, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 What is a function?
blocks.explanation: A function is a rule or correspondence relating two sets so that each element in the first set corresponds to one and only one element in the second set.

book_ref.quote: A function is a rule or correspondence relating two sets in such a way that each element in the first set corresponds to one and only one element in the second set.

blocks.prompt: 2 Express the perimeter \(P\) of a square as a function of its side \(x\), and find \(P(2.5)\).
blocks.explanation: A square has four equal sides, so \(P(x) = 4x\). \(P(2.5) = 4(2.5) = 10\). Each side gives only one perimeter, so \(P\) is a function of \(x\).

book_ref.quote: The area \(A\) of a square depends on one of its sides

blocks.prompt: 3 Define domain, co-domain and range of a function.
blocks.explanation: For \(f : X \to Y\): the domain is the set \(X\) of inputs; the co-domain is the set \(Y\) in which the outputs lie; the range is the set of corresponding elements \(y = f(x)\) actually produced. Range \(\subseteq\) co-domain.

book_ref.quote: is a rule or a correspondence that assigns to each element

blocks.explanation: \(f(-1) = 2\), \(f(0) = 1\), \(f(1) = 2\), \(f(2) = 5\). Range \(= \{1, 2, 5\}\). \(3\) is in the co-domain but no input gives it, so it is not in the range.

book_ref.quote: The set of corresponding elements

blocks.prompt: 8 If \(f(x) = x^{3} - x\), find \(f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\), \(x \ne 0\).
blocks.explanation: \(f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) = \left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^{3} - \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{x^{3}} - \frac{1}{x}\) (\(x \ne 0\) since \(\frac{1}{0}\) is not defined).

book_ref.quote: takes an input \(x\), operates on it in some way and produces exactly one output

blocks.prompt: 9 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 4\).
blocks.explanation: Domain \(= \mathbb{R}\) (no denominator, no root). \(x^{2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 4 \ge 4\), and every \(y \ge 4\) is \(f(\sqrt{y - 4})\): range \(= [4, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = x^{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 10 Find the domain of \(f(x) = \frac{x + 3}{x^{2} - 16}\).
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} - 16 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm 4\), where \(f\) is not defined. Domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{-4, 4\}\).

book_ref.quote: Domain: where is the denominator zero?

blocks.prompt: 11 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \sqrt{25 - x^{2}}\).
blocks.explanation: Need \(25 - x^{2} \ge 0\): critical points \(\pm 5\), test \(x = 0\) (True), \(x = \pm 6\) (False). Domain \(= [-5, 5]\). On it \(0 \le 25 - x^{2} \le 25\), so range \(= [0, 5]\).

book_ref.quote: Condition for a real square root

blocks.prompt: 12 Find the range of \(f(x) = \frac{x}{x^{2} + 1}\).
blocks.explanation: Write \(y = f(x)\) and solve for \(x\).

book_ref.quote: Range: write \(y = f(x)\) and clear the fraction

steps: For \(y \ne 0\): \(x\) is real when \(b^{2} - 4ac = 1 - 4y^{2} \ge 0\), i.e. \(-\frac{1}{2} \le y \le \frac{1}{2}\); \(y = 0\) comes from \(x = 0\).

blocks.prompt: 13 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 2}\).
blocks.explanation: Domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\). \(y = \frac{1}{x - 2} \Rightarrow x = 2 + \frac{1}{y}\), real for every \(y \ne 0\); \(y = 0\) is impossible (numerator \(1 \ne 0\)). Range \(= \mathbb{R} - \{0\}\).

book_ref.quote: Every \(y \ne 0\) gives a real \(x\)

blocks.prompt: 14 State the vertical line test.
blocks.explanation: A graph represents a function if and only if no vertical line intersects the graph more than once. If any vertical line passes through the graph more than once, it is not a function.

book_ref.quote: A graph represents a function if and only if no vertical line intersects the graph more than once.

blocks.prompt: 15 Use the vertical line \(x = 4\) to show that the graph of \(y^{2} = x\) is not the graph of a function of \(x\).
blocks.explanation: For \(x = 4\): \(y^{2} = 4 \Rightarrow y = 2\) or \(y = -2\). The line \(x = 4\) meets the graph at \((4, 2)\) and \((4, -2)\): one input, two outputs, so not a function.

book_ref.quote: If any vertical line passes through the graph more than once, it is not a function.

blocks.prompt: 16 Define a one-to-one function and an onto function.
blocks.explanation: One-to-one: different inputs produce different outputs, i.e. \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2}) \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\). Onto: \(f : X \to Y\) is onto if every \(y \in Y\) has at least one pre-image \(x \in X\) with \(f(x) = y\).

book_ref.quote: A function \(f\) is one-to-one if different inputs produce different outputs

blocks.prompt: 17 Show that \(f(x) = 7x - 2\) is one-to-one.
blocks.explanation: Suppose \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\): \(7x_{1} - 2 = 7x_{2} - 2 \Rightarrow 7x_{1} = 7x_{2} \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\). Hence \(f\) is one-to-one.

book_ref.quote: is one-to-one because \(5x_{1} + 7 = 5x_{2} + 7\)

blocks.prompt: 18 Show that \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = 4x + 1\) is onto.
blocks.explanation: Take any \(y \in \mathbb{R}\). \(y = 4x + 1 \Rightarrow x = \frac{y - 1}{4} \in \mathbb{R}\), and \(f\left(\frac{y - 1}{4}\right) = (y - 1) + 1 = y\). Every \(y\) has a pre-image, so \(f\) is onto.

book_ref.quote: Hence \(f\) is an onto function.

blocks.prompt: 19 Show that \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3\) is not one-to-one.
blocks.explanation: \(f(2) = 4 + 3 = 7\) and \(f(-2) = 4 + 3 = 7\), but \(2 \ne -2\). Two different inputs give the same output, so \(f\) is not one-to-one.

book_ref.quote: Counter-example: not one-to-one

blocks.prompt: 20 Is \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3\) onto? Give a reason.
blocks.explanation: No. \(x^{2} \ge 0\) gives \(f(x) \ge 3\). For example \(2\) has no pre-image: \(x^{2} + 3 = 2 \Rightarrow x^{2} = -1\), no real root. The range \([3, \infty)\) is not the whole co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\).

book_ref.quote: is not the image of any real \(x\)

blocks.prompt: 21 When is a function called bijective? Give an example.
blocks.explanation: \(f : X \to Y\) is bijective if it is both one-to-one and onto. Example: \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x + 1\) (equal outputs force equal inputs, and every \(y\) has the pre-image \(y - 1\)).

book_ref.quote: is called bijective if it is both one-to-one and onto.
A piecewise function is a function that is defined by different expressions

blocks.prompt: 23 What is a point of intersection, and what does it represent?
blocks.explanation: It is a point where two or more graphs meet on the coordinate plane. Its coordinates satisfy every one of the equations, so it represents the solution(s) of the equations of the given functions.

book_ref.quote: The point of intersection is a point where two or more graphs meet on the coordinate plane.

blocks.prompt: 26 Find the point of intersection of \(y = 2x + 3\) and \(y = -x + 9\).

book_ref.quote: The point of intersection of two linear functions is the point where their graphs cross each other.

blocks.prompt: 29 In how many points can a line and a parabola intersect? Explain.
blocks.explanation: At two points, one point or none. Putting the line's y into the parabola gives a quadratic equation, which has two, one or no real roots (discriminant positive, zero or negative). With one point the line is a tangent.

book_ref.quote: A line and a parabola can either intersect at two points, one point or not intersect at all.

blocks.prompt: 33 Show that the line \(y = 2x - 1\) touches the parabola \(y = x^{2}\) at only one point.
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} = 2x - 1 \Rightarrow x^{2} - 2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 1)^{2} = 0\): only \(x = 1\), \(y = 1\). One point \((1, 1)\): the line is a tangent.

blocks.prompt: 34 Find the domain and range of \(y = 3\sqrt{x} + 2\).
blocks.explanation: Domain \(x \ge 0\) (the square root of a negative number is not real). \(\sqrt{x} \ge 0 \Rightarrow 3\sqrt{x} + 2 \ge 2\), with \(y = 2\) at \(x = 0\): range \(y \ge 2\).

book_ref.quote: Graph the square root function

blocks.prompt: 36 Why does the graph of \(y = 2\sqrt{x} + 1\) have no point to the left of the \(y\)-axis?
blocks.explanation: Points to the left of the \(y\)-axis have \(x < 0\), and \(\sqrt{x}\) is not a real number for \(x < 0\). So the domain is \(x \ge 0\) and the graph starts at \((0, 1)\).

blocks.prompt: 37 Find the domain and range of \(y = \sqrt[3]{x + 2}\).
blocks.explanation: Every real number has a real cube root, so the domain is all real numbers. Every \(y\) is reached by \(x = y^{3} - 2\), so the range is all real numbers.

blocks.prompt: 40 What are growth and decay? Give one example of each.
blocks.explanation: Growth: a quantity increases over time, e.g. money in a bank account earning interest. Decay: a quantity decreases over time, e.g. a cup of hot coffee cooling down.

book_ref.quote: When something increases in quantity or size over time, it is called growth.

blocks.prompt: 41 A stock of Rs. 3,000 grows as \(P(t) = 3000e^{0.06t}\). Find its value after 5 years.

book_ref.quote: The value of a stock follows the exponential growth model

blocks.prompt: 42 In how many years does a value growing as \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{0.04t}\) double?
blocks.explanation: \(2P_{0} = P_{0}e^{0.04t} \Rightarrow 2 = e^{0.04t} \Rightarrow \ln 2 = 0.04t \Rightarrow t = \frac{0.6931}{0.04} \approx 17.33\) years.

book_ref.quote: After how many years will the stock double in value?

blocks.prompt: 43 A concentration is \(C(t) = \frac{80}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\) ppm (\(t\) in days). Find \(C(3)\).

book_ref.quote: The concentration of a pollutant in a lake

blocks.prompt: 44 For \(C(t) = \frac{90}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\) ppm, after how many days is the concentration below \(15\) ppm?
blocks.explanation: \(15 = \frac{90}{\sqrt{t + 1}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{t + 1} = 6 \Rightarrow t = 35\). \(C\) decreases as \(t\) grows, so after 35 days it is below \(15\) ppm.

book_ref.quote: After how many days will the concentration drop below 10 ppm?
